kjv: the Lord is with thee (Mary): blessed art thou among women
note: TR adds "eulogemene sy en gynaixin" from Elizabeth's words in 1:42; absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, L, W. The phrase is familiar from the Ave Maria.

kjv: that holy thing which shall be born of thee (Mary)
note: TR adds "ek sou" ("of thee"); absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, A, C, D.

kjv: the dayspring from on high hath visited us
mine: the sunrise from on high will visit us
note: TR aorist "epeskepsato" against future "episkepsetai" in Sinaiticus (first hand) and Vaticanus.

kjv: seeing I (Mary) know not a man
mine: since I (Mary) do not know a man
note: Both keep the Hebraic euphemism (ginosko = sexual relations); modern readers may miss that Mary states she is a virgin.
